title: Paul's defense to the crowd: his conversion retold + his Roman citizenship revealed

paragraphs.text: Brethren and fathers, hear ye the defence which I now make unto you.
paragraphs.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νυνὶ ἀπολογίας.
paragraphs.translit: Andres adelphoi kai pateres, akousate mou tēs pros hymas nyni apologias.

paragraphs.text: And when they heard that he spake unto them in the Hebrew language, they were the more quiet: and he saith,
paragraphs.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ὅτι τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ προσεφώνει αὐτοῖς μᾶλλον παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν. καὶ φησίν·
paragraphs.translit: Akousantes de hoti tē Hebraidi dialektō prosephōnei autois mallon pareschon hēsychian. kai phēsin·

paragraphs.text: I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city, at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict manner of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as ye all are this day:
paragraphs.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος, γεγεννημένος ἐν Ταρσῷ τῆς Κιλικίας, ἀνατεθραμμένος δὲ ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ, πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τοῦ πατρῴου νόμου, ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ θεοῦ καθὼς πάντες ὑμεῖς ἐστε σήμερον,
paragraphs.translit: Egō eimi anēr Ioudaios, gegennēmenos en Tarsō tēs Kilikias, anatethrammenos de en tē polei tautē para tous podas Gamaliēl, pepaideumenos kata akribeian tou patrōou nomou, zēlōtēs hyparchōn tou theou kathōs pantes hymeis este sēmeron,

paragraphs.text: and I persecuted this Way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
paragraphs.original: ὃς ταύτην τὴν ὁδὸν ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου, δεσμεύων καὶ παραδιδοὺς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας,
paragraphs.translit: hos tautēn tēn hodon ediōxa achri thanatou, desmeuōn kai paradidous eis phylakas andras te kai gynaikas,

paragraphs.text: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and journeyed to Damascus to bring them also that were there unto Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.
paragraphs.original: ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον· παρʼ ὧν καὶ ἐπιστολὰς δεξάμενος πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἰς Δαμασκὸν ἐπορευόμην ἄξων καὶ τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας δεδεμένους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hōs kai ho archiereus martyrei moi kai pan to presbyterion· parʼ hōn kai epistolas dexamenos pros tous adelphous eis Damaskon eporeuomēn axōn kai tous ekeise ontas dedemenous eis Ierousalēm hina timōrēthōsin.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and drew nigh unto Damascus, about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι τῇ Δαμασκῷ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ἐξαίφνης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιαστράψαι φῶς ἱκανὸν περὶ ἐμέ,
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de moi poreuomenō kai engizonti tē Damaskō peri mesēmbrian exaiphnēs ek tou ouranou periastrapsai phōs hikanon peri eme,

paragraphs.text: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
paragraphs.original: ἔπεσά τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
paragraphs.translit: epesa te eis to edaphos kai ēkousa phōnēs legousēs moi· Saoul Saoul, ti me diōkeis;

paragraphs.text: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπεκρίθην· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; εἶπέν τε πρὸς ἐμέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις.
paragraphs.translit: egō de apekrithēn· Tis ei, kyrie; eipen te pros eme· Egō eimi Iēsous ho Nazōraios hon sy diōkeis.

paragraphs.text: And they that were with me beheld indeed the light, but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες τὸ μὲν φῶς ἐθεάσαντο τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de syn emoi ontes to men phōs etheasanto tēn de phōnēn ouk ēkousan tou lalountos moi.

paragraphs.text: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
paragraphs.original: εἶπον δέ· Τί ποιήσω, κύριε; ὁ δὲ κύριος εἶπεν πρός με· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου εἰς Δαμασκόν, κἀκεῖ σοι λαληθήσεται περὶ πάντων ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: eipon de· Ti poiēsō, kyrie; ho de kyrios eipen pros me· Anastas poreuou eis Damaskon, kakei soi lalēthēsetai peri pantōn hōn tetaktai soi poiēsai.

paragraphs.text: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me I came into Damascus.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου, χειραγωγούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν συνόντων μοι ἦλθον εἰς Δαμασκόν.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de ouk eneblepon apo tēs doxēs tou phōtos ekeinou, cheiragōgoumenos hypo tōn synontōn moi ēlthon eis Damaskon.

paragraphs.text: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews that dwelt there,
paragraphs.original: Ἁνανίας δέ τις ἀνὴρ εὐλαβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον μαρτυρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων Ἰουδαίων,
paragraphs.translit: Hananias de tis anēr eulabēs kata ton nomon martyroumenos hypo pantōn tōn katoikountōn Ioudaiōn,

paragraphs.text: came unto me, and standing by me said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And in that very hour I looked up on him.
paragraphs.original: ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἐμὲ καὶ ἐπιστὰς εἶπέν μοι· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ἀνάβλεψον· κἀγὼ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἀνέβλεψα εἰς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: elthōn pros eme kai epistas eipen moi· Saoul adelphe, anablepson· kagō autē tē hōra aneblepsa eis auton.

paragraphs.text: And he said, The God of our fathers hath appointed thee to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν τὸν δίκαιον καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen· Ho theos tōn paterōn hēmōn proecheirisato se gnōnai to thelēma autou kai idein ton dikaion kai akousai phōnēn ek tou stomatos autou,

paragraphs.text: For thou shalt be a witness for him unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἔσῃ μάρτυς αὐτῷ πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἑώρακας καὶ ἤκουσας.
paragraphs.translit: hoti esē martys autō pros pantas anthrōpous hōn heōrakas kai ēkousas.

paragraphs.text: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on his name.
paragraphs.original: καὶ νῦν τί μέλλεις; ἀναστὰς βάπτισαι καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai nyn ti melleis; anastas baptisai kai apolousai tas hamartias sou epikalesamenos to onoma autou.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, that, when I had returned to Jerusalem, and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance,
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι ὑποστρέψαντι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ προσευχομένου μου ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de moi hypostrepsanti eis Ierousalēm kai proseuchomenou mou en tō hierō genesthai me en ekstasei

paragraphs.text: and saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem; because they will not receive of thee testimony concerning me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν λέγοντά μοι· Σπεῦσον καὶ ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἰερουσαλήμ, διότι οὐ παραδέξονταί σου μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idein auton legonta moi· Speuson kai exelthe en tachei ex Ierousalēm, dioti ou paradexontai sou martyrian peri emou.

paragraphs.text: And I said, Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
paragraphs.original: κἀγὼ εἶπον· Κύριε, αὐτοὶ ἐπίστανται ὅτι ἐγὼ ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τοὺς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ σέ·
paragraphs.translit: kagō eipon· Kyrie, autoi epistantai hoti egō ēmēn phylakizōn kai derōn kata tas synagōgas tous pisteuontas epi se·

paragraphs.text: and when the blood of Stephen thy witness was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting, and keeping the garments of them that slew him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐξεχύννετο τὸ αἷμα Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤμην ἐφεστὼς καὶ συνευδοκῶν καὶ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια τῶν ἀναιρούντων αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hote exechynneto to haima Stephanou tou martyros sou, kai autos ēmēn ephestōs kai syneudokōn kai phylassōn ta himatia tōn anairountōn auton.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee forth far hence unto the Gentiles.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρός με· Πορεύου, ὅτι ἐγὼ εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστελῶ σε.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen pros me· Poreuou, hoti egō eis ethnē makran exapostelō se.

paragraphs.text: And they gave him audience unto this word; and they lifted up their voice, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
paragraphs.original: Ἤκουον δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου καὶ ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν λέγοντες· Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον, οὐ γὰρ καθῆκεν αὐτὸν ζῆν.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkouon de autou achri toutou tou logou kai epēran tēn phōnēn autōn legontes· Aire apo tēs gēs ton toiouton, ou gar kathēken auton zēn.

paragraphs.text: And as they cried out, and threw off their garments, and cast dust into the air,
paragraphs.original: κραυγαζόντων τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα,
paragraphs.translit: kraugazontōn te autōn kai rhiptountōn ta himatia kai koniorton ballontōn eis ton aera,

paragraphs.text: the chief captain commanded him be brought into the castle, bidding that he should be examined by scourging, that he might know for what cause they so shouted against him.
paragraphs.original: ἐκέλευσεν ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν, εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ διʼ ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ekeleusen ho chiliarchos eisagesthai auton eis tēn parembolēn, eipas mastixin anetazesthai auton hina epignō diʼ hēn aitian houtōs epephōnoun autō.

paragraphs.text: And when they had tied him up with the thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος· Εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν;
paragraphs.translit: hōs de proeteinan auton tois himasin eipen pros ton hestōta hekatontarchon ho Paulos· Ei anthrōpon Rhōmaion kai akatakriton exestin hymin mastizein;

paragraphs.text: And when the centurion heard it, he went to the chief captain and told him, saying, What art thou about to do? for this man is a Roman.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν λέγων· Τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν; ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: akousas de ho hekatontarchēs proselthōn tō chiliarchō apēngeilen legōn· Ti melleis poiein; ho gar anthrōpos houtos Rhōmaios estin.

paragraphs.text: And the chief captain came and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? And he said, Yea.
paragraphs.original: προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Λέγε μοι, σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ; ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ναί.
paragraphs.translit: proselthōn de ho chiliarchos eipen autō· Lege moi, sy Rhōmaios ei; ho de ephē· Nai.

paragraphs.text: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this citizenship. And Paul said, But I am [a Roman] born.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος· Ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην. ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη· Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē de ho chiliarchos· Egō pollou kephalaiou tēn politeian tautēn ektēsamēn. ho de Paulos ephē· Egō de kai gegennēmai.

paragraphs.text: They then that were about to examine him straightway departed from him: and the chief captain also was afraid when he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
paragraphs.original: εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν· καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν ἦν δεδεκώς.
paragraphs.translit: eutheōs oun apestēsan apʼ autou hoi mellontes auton anetazein· kai ho chiliarchos de ephobēthē epignous hoti Rhōmaios estin kai hoti auton ēn dedekōs.

paragraphs.text: But on the morrow, desiring to know the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
paragraphs.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔλυσεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκέλευσεν συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ πᾶν τὸ συνέδριον, καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Tē de epaurion boulomenos gnōnai to asphales to ti katēgoreitai hypo tōn Ioudaiōn elysen auton, kai ekeleusen synelthein tous archiereis kai pan to synedrion, kai katagagōn ton Paulon estēsen eis autous.
